;;;; Batch processing. Stubs make the file loadable.

(defpackage #:kc6.batch (:use #:cl))
(in-package #:kc6.batch)

(defun acquire-lock (lock) lock)
(defun release-lock (lock) lock)
(defun stage (item) item)
(defun flush-staged () t)

(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (dolist (item items)
    (stage item))
  (flush-staged)
  (release-lock lock))

(defun read-forms (path)
  (with-open-file (in path)
    (loop for form = (read in nil in) until (eq form in) collect form)))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(defun tree-count (needle tree)
  (cond ((equal needle tree) 1)
        ((consp tree) (+ (tree-count needle (car tree)) (tree-count needle (cdr tree))))
        (t 0)))

(let* ((forms (handler-case (read-forms "batch.lisp")
                (error (c) (fail (format nil "batch.lisp does not read: ~a" c)))))
       (pb (find-if (lambda (f) (and (consp f) (eq (first f) 'defun)
                                     (eq (second f) 'process-batch)))
                    forms))
       (body (cdddr pb)))
  (unless pb (fail "process-batch is gone"))
  (unless (equal (first body) '(acquire-lock lock))
    (fail "acquire-lock must stay first, OUTSIDE the protection"))
  (unless (= 2 (length body)) (fail "body should be acquire then one unwind-protect"))
  (let ((up (second body)))
    (unless (and (consp up) (eq (first up) 'unwind-protect)) (fail "no unwind-protect"))
    (let ((protected (second up)) (cleanups (cddr up)))
      (unless (equal cleanups '((release-lock lock)))
        (fail (format nil "cleanup is ~s, want ((release-lock lock))" cleanups)))
      (unless (plusp (tree-count '(stage item) protected)) (fail "staging left the protected form"))
      (unless (plusp (tree-count '(flush-staged) protected)) (fail "flush left the protected form"))
      (when (plusp (tree-count '(release-lock lock) protected))
        (fail "release-lock also appears inside the protected form")))))
(format t "ok~%")

The task is clear. I need to restructure process-batch:

```lisp
(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (unwind-protect
       (progn
         (dolist (item items)
           (stage item))
         (flush-staged))
    (release-lock lock)))
```

Let me check the check.lisp requirements:
- `(first body)` must equal `(acquire-lock lock)` — body is `(cdddr pb)`, i.e., after `(defun process-batch (items lock) ...)`, so body = the forms in the body.
- `(= 2 (length body))` — body should be acquire then one unwind-protect.
- `(second body)` must be an unwind-protect.
- cleanups = `(cddr up)` must equal `'((release-lock lock))`.
- protected = `(second up)` must contain `(stage item)` and `(flush-staged)`.
- `(release-lock lock)` must not appear inside the protected form.

So the protected form needs to contain both `(stage item)` (inside the dolist) and `(flush-staged)`. A single `progn` containing the dolist and flush-staged works.

The check requires the body to be exactly two forms (acquire, then one `unwind-protect`), so the staging and flushing need to be inside a single protected form (a `progn`).

`./check` exits 0. The restructure is complete:

```lisp
(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (unwind-protect
       (progn
         (dolist (item items)
           (stage item))
         (flush-staged))
    (release-lock lock)))
```

- `acquire-lock` stays first, outside the protection.
- Everything between acquire and release (the `dolist`/`stage` loop and `flush-staged`) is the protected form of a single `unwind-protect`.
- `(release-lock lock)` appears exactly once, as the cleanup, so it runs on every exit — normal or signaled.
